| EXPR.DSF | BLANK_EN.DSF's skeleton (DRC, by Uto) plus two added `#define`s and one added process, by this project | GPL-3.0 | Quoted-expression operand coverage: after the existing `#define fGFlags` line, `#define EPI "pi"` (a #define-position quoted expression, evaluating to 3 via trunc toward zero) and `#define ESHADOW 7`; before `/END` a new `/PRO 7` with one entry running SET across seventeen quoted/plain expressions - arithmetic (`1+2`, `2+3*4`, `7/2`, `(1+2)*3`), a symbol reference (`COLS+1`), functions (`sqrt(16)`, `trunc(3.9)`), radix literals (`$FF`, `%101`, `&17`), a float literal (`1e2`), a bitwise op (`12 and 10`), control functions (`if(1=1,5,6)`, `case(2,99,1,10,2,20)`), the two new `#define`s (`ESHADOW*2`, `EPI+1`), and an indirected `SET @"1+2"` - plus a trailing `#db "1+2"` directive on the same entry. The quoted `#db` expression is the reference's untouched MAXLONGINT filler rather than its evaluated value 3 (the queued byte comes from the lexer's int-value slot, never updated for a string token, not from the range-checked expression result), so the golden carries `"Opcode":2147483647` for that leg. Values chosen to land within SET's 0..255 parameter range on every target (COLS+1 <= 91 <= 255 everywhere). Confirmed against a live reference drf.exe + drb.php compile before committing - both accepted the quoted `#db` cleanly. Column layout is spaces, not tabs, matching both BLANK_EN.DSF's and CONDACTS.DSF's own entry formatting (neither file uses a literal tab byte anywhere); the `#db` line sits after `DONE` in the same entry, the general directive-follows-a-condact placement documented for `#defb`/CALL pairs (no existing fixture has a `#db`/`#defb` line to match column-for-column, CONDACTS.DSF included). CRLF-bearing like every other .DSF fixture here |

| IFDEFS.DSF | BLANK_EN.DSF's skeleton (DRC, by Uto) plus one added `#define` and one added process, by this project | GPL-3.0 | Conditional-compilation coverage: after the existing `#define fGFlags` line, `#define USERSYM 1`; before `/END` a new `/PRO 7` with seven `#ifdef`/`#ifndef`-gated entries, each a one-condact `SET n` / `DONE` pair so the entry table itself - not message/text tables - shifts per branch: `#ifdef "NEXTDAAD"` (SET 10), `#ifdef "BIT8"` (SET 11), `#ifdef "BIT16"` (SET 12), `#ifndef "BIT8"` (SET 13), `#ifdef "USERSYM"` / `#else` (SET 14 / SET 15), `#ifdef "NOSUCHSYM"` (SET 16, a symbol defined nowhere), `#ifdef "CLIONLY"` (SET 17, a symbol defined nowhere in the DSF - only a `drf.exe`/`ndrc --to-json` additional-symbols argument supplies it). The directive's symbol MUST be quoted (`#ifdef "NEXTDAAD"`, not `#ifdef NEXTDAAD`) - USintactic.pas:267/sintactic.c:520-522 reject an unquoted label with "please include the label or expression in between quotes"; confirmed live against reference drf.exe before committing. `#ifdef`/`#ifndef`/`#endif`/`#else` are transparent at the token-stream level (USintactic.pas Scan/SkipBlock, ported at sintactic.c:408-439/450-534) - they execute during Scan() itself regardless of what grammar production is calling it, so wrapping whole `>`-entries (not just condact lines) works identically to wrapping a mid-entry fragment. Observable entry sets measured live: NEXTDAAD compiles {10, 11, 14} (NEXTDAAD and BIT8 both defined for that target since drf.pas:243; BIT16 undefined; USERSYM from the fixture's own `#define`), PC VGA compiles {12, 13, 14} (BIT16 defined, BIT8 undefined), HTML compiles {13, 14} (neither BIT8 nor BIT16 defined - drf.pas:245's comment: "Please notice HTML target adds neither BIT8 nor BIT16 symbols."); no target compiles 15 (USERSYM is always defined here), 16 (NOSUCHSYM never defined) or 17 (CLIONLY) without the CLI symbol. A `NEXTDAAD` run with an additional-symbols argument of `CLIONLY` (drf.pas:354/drf.pas:41's syntax note) compiles {10, 11, 14, 17}, confirming the `#ifdef CLIONLY` leg without committing that JSON (Task 8's concern). Column layout is spaces, not tabs, matching BLANK_EN.DSF's own convention (`>` col 0, first `_` col 2, second `_` col 10, opcode col 16); CRLF-bearing like every other .DSF fixture here |

| BADSYNTAX.DSF | BLANK_EN.DSF's skeleton (DRC, by Uto) plus one deliberately invalid line, by this project | GPL-3.0 | PURPOSE: the standing deliberately-invalid fixture (owner-approved) that keeps the `--to-json` matrix's expected-failure "pass-as-pin" path under permanent live exercise - the 840-cell matrix otherwise has zero cells where the reference itself fails, so that machinery ran only in tamper tests. A byte-copy of BLANK_EN.DSF with one garbage line, `- BADSYNTAX FIXTURE: deliberately invalid line, do not fix.`, spliced in immediately before the `/CTL` section. The leading `-` is not followed by a digit, so DSF.l's `-?[0-9]+` rule cannot match it and it falls through to the catch-all `.` rule (DSF.l:57, USintactic.pas:49-54's LexerError/SyntaxError, Halt(1)) - an unconditional lexer error hit during the very first token scan, before any target-specific processing, so it is TARGET- and VERSION-independent. Measured live against reference `drf.exe` 0.40 on NEXTDAAD v3, PC VGA v3, HTML v2 and ZX 48K v2 before wiring it into the matrix: all four produced the identical `64:2:g.DSF: Unexpected character or string: "-".`, exit code 1, and neither wrote a `g.json`; `ndrc --to-json` reproduces the same text/exit code/no-JSON on all four, and across the full 35 target/subtarget pairs x 2 versions (70 cells) in the matrix deck. This fixture must NEVER be "fixed" - a clean compile here would silently delete the matrix's only live pin exercise. It has no `--from-json` golden (it never compiles), so it is absent from `gen_goldens.py`'s `curated_jobs()` and carries no committed `tests/fixtures/*.json` - only `TO_JSON_DECK` in `tests/oracle/verify.py` exercises it |

## Not committed, deliberately

Rabenstein, Urban Upstart and Dracula DSFs are
third-party games. A golden DDB built from one is a derivative work of
that game, so neither the source nor its goldens may be committed here.
They stay useful as a local-only corpus: pass their paths to
`run_reference` directly to compile them through the reference
toolchain. There is no configured corpus hook for them - they are not
picked up by the test matrix and have no goldens.
